title: Senior Pre-Sales Systems Engineer, Higher Education (Texas)
description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work-work that changes the world-is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

Everpure (formerly Pure Storage) is hiring a Senior Pre-Sales Systems Engineer to support our Higher Education business, with a focus on R1 research universities.

R1 institutions are not one customer. A single campus can behave like a dozen different organizations at the same time: central IT running enterprise applications, research computing and HPC teams, genomics and imaging cores, AI and machine learning labs competing for GPU time, an academic medical center with its own rules and its own budget, and faculty groups buying infrastructure directly with grant money. Decisions move through CIOs, research computing directors, principal investigators, sponsored programs offices, procurement, and consortium contract vehicles, often in parallel and not always in agreement.

That environment rewards someone who can hold a lot of context at once, translate between very different audiences, and connect technology to the outcomes these institutions actually care about: time to result for researchers, compliance with sponsor and grant requirements, data that stays usable for a decade or more, and budgets that have to stretch further every year.

You will be the technical lead on these accounts, working alongside account managers, specialists, and partners to build solutions customers can defend internally, both technically and financially.

Location: Austin, Texas

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Develop a real understanding of what drives each institution: research priorities, funding cycles, capital versus operating constraints, and who actually makes the decision

• Connect technology, including the Everpure portfolio and the broader ecosystem, to measurable research and institutional outcomes

• Move fluently between principal investigators, research computing staff, central IT, CIOs, finance, and procurement, adapting the conversation to each audience instead of delivering the same presentation

• Build the business case alongside the technical one: total cost of ownership, power and cooling, data center footprint, staff time, and the real cost of the current environment

• Support research workloads end to end, from instrument and sequencer output through HPC and AI pipelines to long-term retention and archive

• Help customers work through data management questions: lifecycle and retention, reproducibility, sponsor and funding agency data sharing expectations, research data governance, and security requirements such as NIST 800-171 and CMMC where they apply

• Partner closely with account managers, specialists, channel partners, and higher education purchasing consortia and contract vehicles

• Take ownership of evaluations, benchmarks, proofs of concept, and system configurations, and secure the technical win

• Capture requirements and translate them into solutions that help institutions grow their research capability rather than just their capacity

• Author responses to RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs, which in this segment are frequent and detailed

• Stay current on the competitive landscape and make sure our positioning reflects it honestly

• Follow market and research computing trends closely enough to bring that thinking back into our organization

• Lead by example living the Pure Values: Persistence, Creativity, Teamwork, Ownership and Customer-first

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Required:

• 8 or more years of relevant experience across technology, solution design, and customer-facing communication

title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer

ABOUT ANTITHESIS

We take cutting edge software-testing technologies and make them useful for finding real bugs in our customer’s software, allowing them to make more reliable software and ship with confidence.

Historically we’ve focused on the hardest testing problems, providing deterministic simulation testing of whole distributed systems, finding and helping people to understand bugs that would have been a nightmare to find in production.

As more and more code is written by agents, everyone is starting to realise just how important software verification is, and we’re in the process of expanding the problems and companies we target, and are providing an increasingly broad suite of open source and commercial testing tools for a much wider variety of problems and audiences.

We’re well funded, deeply technical, and committed to improving the quality of software across the board. If you’d like to help us do that, we’d love to hear from you.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'd be joining a small London-based team building out a new Antithesis product, focusing on a more downmarket and diverse set of customers than our main product. We’re rapidly iterating and expect to be shipping some time early in the new year.

We're looking for an engineer at the Senior to Staff level to help us make that system dependable. This will be “devops” in the traditional sense, though more dev than ops: You'll be a member of the engineering team, not a separate operations function, working in the same repository as everyone else, but your primary area of responsibility will be how the system runs in production. That means AWS, deployment, observability, alerting, and the on-call that comes with them.

There will be some on-call, shared with the rest of the team, and part of the job will be helping us define how that works. This is the first product Antithesis is shipping primarily out of the UK, and we want to get things right from the start to make it sustainable and quiet. We’re thinking of this role as less about being the person that gets paged, and more being the person who tries to make sure that nobody does.

Likely much of this will have already been prototyped by the time you join, but there will be a lot of latitude to make big changes to how that works.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own our AWS environment.

- Define and build out our observability and alerting

- Ensure our continuous deployment story is robust and stress-free in an environment where we expect to change production many times a day.

- Build and maintain our infrastructure for our fleet of testing VMs for running customers’ code.

- Take charge of our incident response and make sure we learn from incidents so we don’t repeat them.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

An ideal candidate would have most of the following:

- You have been responsible for a production system on AWS, including being on call for it, and you have opinions about what you would do differently.

- Fluency with infrastructure as code and CI/CD.

- Practical experience of observability.

- You have built alerting that people trusted.

- Experience operating Postgres: backups, upgrades, migrations, and what happens when they go wrong.

- Solid Linux, container and networking fundamentals.

- You are comfortable directing AI coding agents and sceptical of what they produce.

Bonus:

- Experience running agentic systems in production.

- Sandboxing or isolating untrusted code (microVMs, gVisor, or similar), or security work on a multi-tenant platform.

- Being the first infrastructure engineer on a team, or building an on-call rotation from nothing.

- Cost management for bursty, compute-heavy workloads.

- Nix.

ABOUT OUR TEAM

Our team spans CS degrees, philosophy, mathematics, everything in between, or nothing formal at all. What everyone shares is a high bar for engineering quality. We work primarily in-person because it's how we build trust and tackle hard problems together.

title: Responsable d'équipe exploitation assainissement (GISA) H/F
description: Rejoignez un acteur majeur du service public de l'eau et de l’assainissement ! Au sein de notre Centre d'Exploitation de La Gorgue, vous pilotez l'activité d’exploitation des ouvrages de collecte et de traitement des eaux usées sur le territoire couvrant 19 communes adhérentes à la compétence assainissement collectif, dans le secteur des Flandres intérieurs et de la Pévèle. Véritable manager de proximité, vous coordonnez les équipes et les moyens techniques afin de garantir la performance des installations, la conformité réglementaire et la préservation de l'environnement. Rattaché à l’Adjoint technique assainissement, vos missions seront les suivantes : Pilotage de l'exploitation assainissement Garantir le bon fonctionnement des ouvrages d'assainissement : stations d'épuration, stations de relèvement, lagunages, bassins de stockage-restitution et réseaux. Superviser les performances des installations et analyser les données d'exploitation. Veiller au respect des obligations réglementaires et des exigences d'autosurveillance. Assurer le suivi des indicateurs techniques et environnementaux. Organiser et coordonner les interventions préventives et curatives.
